extracted.intended_audience: Patent owners, third-party reexamination requesters, and patent practitioners preparing requests for ex parte or inter partes reexamination at the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and filing ex parte and inter partes reexamination requests to satisfy 37 CFR 1.510 and 1.915, with best practices to obtain a filing date and facilitate examiner review. Covers SNQ statements, proposed rejections, required forms, service, signatures, and document/formatting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: File electronically
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for reexamination may be filed as 'new applications' in EFS-Web (select New applications → utility or design → type 'Reexam' and designate ex parte or inter partes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic filing avoids mail/scanning delays, makes the request visible more quickly, and expedites internal handling. Use the EFS-Web document code spreadsheet (link provided) and contact CRU customer service or the Electronic Business Center for help with codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use correct forms and include detailed request
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form PTO/SB/57 for ex parte requests and PTO/SB/58 for inter partes requests, in addition to an attached detailed request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms are available on the USPTO Patent Forms page. Inclusion of the form plus a clearly organized detailed request simplifies review and reduces chance of defect identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include the correct fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the complete reexamination fee with the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee amounts are subject to change; check the USPTO Fee Schedule. Lack of the correct fee is a filing-date defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a legible copy of the patent to be reexamined (and related certificates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a copy of the patent to be reexamined including any disclaimer(s), certificate(s) of correction or prior reexamination certificate(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a legible copy of the entire patent (front face, drawings, specification/claims in double column format), each page plainly written on only one side. Illegible copies are not accepted. For non-English references provide translations of relevant portions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and legibility for submitted papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents filed will be scanned/entered into the image file wrapper system; ensure legibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid small type (below 12 point), colors, photographs and small detailed drawings that do not scan well. Use line spacing of at least 1.5 and single-sided pages to ensure scanned text is legible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a clear Statement of a Substantial New Question of Patentability (SNQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each SNQ, state concisely the new technological teaching provided by at least one patent or publication cited for that SNQ, and explain how it presents a new, non-cumulative teaching for the claims at issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify what the new technological teaching is or how the reference is presented in a 'new light' for every claim for which reexamination is requested. Provide citations to specific portions of references. Do not attempt to identify every claim limitation as the new teaching (this can obscure the SNQ). State whether the reference was previously considered and to what extent. Provide SNQ statements separate from the detailed proposed rejections. See MPEP §§2216/2616.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify every claim for which reexamination is requested
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an identification of every claim that is the subject of the reexamination request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state which claims are applicable to each proposed rejection; do not use phrases like 'at least claims 1 and 2.' Proper claim identification is part of filing-date compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: State clearly each and every Proposed Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Do NOT lump multiple proposed rejections based on different grounds; state each proposed rejection explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate anticipation (35 U.S.C. 102) explanations from obviousness (35 U.S.C. 103) explanations; separate alternative primary/secondary teachings; avoid 'and/or' and footnote 'suggestions' of other rejections. Group multiple claims under the same ground where appropriate (e.g., 'claims 1-4, 6, 8, and 12 should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) as anticipated by Smith'). For patent-owner requests, clearly state which references apply to which claims and identify what elements are or are not shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a Detailed Explanation for each Proposed Rejection or Application of the Art
rubrics_metrics.description: For each proposed rejection (or, for patent owners, each application of the art), provide a separate, detailed explanation showing how the references apply to every claim limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For every limitation: (1) point out how the reference meets/teaches the limitation, or (2) for patent-owner requests state that the limitation is not covered, or (3) admit the limitation is known where applicable. For dependent claims, show how prior art applies to added limitations and refer to explanations of base claims. For obviousness, explain what the primary reference teaches, what it fails to teach, how other prior art supplies missing limitations, and why a person of ordinary skill would combine them (provide a reason). Use either a claim chart OR prose (not both), keep explanations consistent with the proposed rejection, and include only the claims and references listed in the proposed rejection. Ensure an explanation only addresses anticipation when the basis is 102 and only addresses obviousness when the basis is 103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim chart vs narrative: provide one clear format
rubrics_metrics.description: The detailed explanation must be in claim chart or prose (narrative) format — do not provide both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing both inflates length and risks inconsistencies; pick one format and be consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite only documents that form the basis of proposed rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: List on the citation form (PTO/SB/08, PTO/SB/42, PTO-1449, or equivalent) ONLY the patents and publications that form the basis of the proposed rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT include litigation or background documents on the listing. If a 'background' document is discussed in the detailed explanation as part of a proposed rejection, it must be listed and provided as a basis for the proposed rejection. Avoid including documents that are not a basis for any proposed rejection, because listing unsubstantiated documents may cause noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide copies and translations of cited references
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a copy of each and every reference that is cited (except U.S. patent documents); provide English translations for non-English patents/printed publications (at least relevant portions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legible copies only — illegible copies will not be accepted and will be deemed not received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service when requester is not the patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: A third-party requester must serve the Request and all related papers on the patent owner at the correspondence address in the patent file (37 CFR 1.33(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check PAIR for the current address of record. If service was not possible, supply a duplicate copy to the Office with a factual explanation of efforts to effect service. Include the name and address of the party served in the certificate of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include power of attorney or representative status when filing for another party
rubrics_metrics.description: If an attorney/agent files the request and identifies another party on whose behalf the request is filed, attach a power of attorney or show that the attorney/agent is acting under 37 CFR 1.34.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/81B may be used to record a third-party requester power of attorney; use forms for change of address as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify real party-in-interest and required inter partes certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: For inter partes reexamination: identify the real party or parties in interest and make the required certification that the estoppel provisions of 37 CFR 1.907 do not prohibit the requested inter partes proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also confirm the patent issued from an application filed on or after November 29, 1999 (otherwise inter partes reexamination cannot be used). See MPEP 2611.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update correspondence address in the patent file
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners must ensure the correspondence address in the patent file is current (correspondence is sent to the address in the file).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 2222. Failure to update may prevent receipt of USPTO communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properly sign the Request
rubrics_metrics.description: The Request itself (not just the transmittal or cover letter) must be signed by a patent practitioner under 37 CFR 1.34 or by a person authorized to act on behalf of the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure the signature complies with 37 CFR 1.4(d)(1) for handwritten signatures or 37 CFR 1.4(d)(2) for s-signatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid including prohibited or extraneous statutory arguments/information
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful of statutory constraints — do not include certain types of information in a reexamination request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT include comments alleging misconduct (e.g., inequitable conduct), litigation arguments beyond bare notice (notification of litigation must be limited to bare notice without arguments; see MPEP 2282 and 2686), proposed rejections based on lack of utility or enablement under 35 U.S.C. 101, proposed rejections based on 35 U.S.C. 112, or proposed rejections based on prior use or prior knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure proposed rejections resolve the identified SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposed rejection (or application of the art) should unambiguously include at least one new technical teaching from the SNQ section so that a decision on the proposed rejection will resolve the SNQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a proposed rejection does not include a reference that raises an asserted SNQ, the request may be identified as noncompliant because it is not apparent how the proposed rejection will resolve the SNQ (e.g., a 102 rejection based on reference B will not resolve an SNQ raised by reference A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly state the statutory basis for each proposed rejection and avoid vague groupings
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify whether references are applied under 35 U.S.C. 102 or 35 U.S.C. 103 and explain each proposed rejection separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate 102 and 103 explanations; avoid statements like 'Reference A also makes Claim 1 obvious' without detailed obviousness reasoning. Avoid alternate cumulative references grouped with 'and/or' — separately explain each combination you propose (e.g., A in view of C; B in view of C), and avoid headings that suggest additional unexplained rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid common defects: distinguish SNQ from detailed explanation and do not lump references
rubrics_metrics.description: Common initial defects include failing to distinguish an SNQ from the detailed explanation, grouping references without separate explanations, or citing references that are not discussed in the detailed description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement pointing out an SNQ should focus solely on the new technical teaching. The detailed explanation should provide the proposed rejection that includes that teaching. Too much extraneous law or whole proposed rejections in the SNQ section obscures the SNQ; be concise and focussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include both extensive general case law and your facts mixed together
rubrics_metrics.description: Restating large blocks of general case law or MPEP sections is not helpful unless tied to particular facts of the reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long citations of general case law increase length and risk burying specific facts. If necessary, place extended legal discussion in a separate section without facts specific to the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedite processing: avoid filing as follow-on paper in the patent file
rubrics_metrics.description: New requests for reexamination must be filed as 'new applications' in EFS-Web or as a request in paper, and not as follow-on papers in the patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow-on papers can be misfiled or mislabeled; filing electronically as a new application reduces delay and increases visibility in the image file wrapper system. If filed in paper, processing delays may make the request invisible for weeks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize submission with clear headings and include required items under clear headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of required items (fee, SNQ statement, claim identification, detailed explanation, copies of references, etc.) with appropriate and clear headings simplifies review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear headings help USPTO support staff, examiners, patent owners, and the public and reduce likelihood of defect identification or denial of reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid loose ends in headers or summaries that are not later explained
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not summarize or list multiple alternative rejections in a heading unless each is separately and fully explained in the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A header like 'Claim 1 is unpatentable over references A and/or B in view of C and/or D' must be followed by explanations covering each variant the header suggests. Unexplained variants can cause the request to be found defective.
